flow.zh: 杉林溪的雲霧是一首歌

flow.caption_zh: 衫林溪的雲霧是一首歌.  台灣南投竹山鎮。

zh: 台灣杉林溪森林生態渡假園區位於南投縣竹山鎮與鹿谷鄉交界，海拔約1,600 公尺，
是一處結合原始森林、生態保育與高山休閒的著名山林園區。園區終年雲霧繚繞、
氣候涼爽。杉林溪以豐富的針闊葉混合林相聞名，杉木、紅檜、台灣扁柏與楓香交錯
成林，四季景色分明：春賞櫻花與牡丹，夏觀瀑布飛泉，秋看楓紅層層，冬季則有
霧淞與山嵐之美。園區內的松瀧岩瀑布、天地眼、青龍瀑布等自然景觀，展現高山
水文與地質演化的壯麗氣勢。 杉林溪也是重要的生態教育基地，棲息著多種鳥類、
昆蟲與台灣特有植物，園區設有完善的步道系統與解說設施，讓遊客在漫步林間時，
得以親近自然、理解山林的生命律動。  (整理自南投旅遊網)
en: Taiwan's Shanlinsi Forest Recreation Area lies on the border of Zhushan Township and Lugu Township in Nantou County, at an elevation of about 1,600 meters,
It is a renowned mountain forest park combining primeval forest, ecological conservation, and alpine leisure. The park is wreathed in cloud and mist year-round,
The climate is cool. Shanlinxi is renowned for its rich mixed coniferous-broadleaf forest, where cedar, red cypress, Taiwan cypress, and sweetgum interweave
forming forests, with four seasons clearly distinct: cherry blossoms and peonies in spring, cascading waterfalls in summer, layered red maples in autumn, and in winter there is
The beauty of rime frost and mountain mist. Natural sights within the park such as Songlong Rock Falls, the Eye of Heaven and Earth, and Qinglong Falls display the high mountain's
the majestic grandeur of hydrological and geological evolution. Shanlinxi is also an important base for ecological education, home to many species of birds,
insects and plants endemic to Taiwan; the park is equipped with a complete trail system and interpretive facilities, so that visitors strolling through the forest,
able to draw close to nature and understand the living rhythm of the mountain forest. (Compiled from the Nantou Tourism website)

zh: 衫林溪的雲霧，讓我想起
蘇格蘭高地起伏的青翠山坡
環湖山勢的倒影，讓我想起
紐西蘭南島壯麗的峽灣岬角
岬角的波浪，讓我想起
野柳雲天下孤立的女王岩
女王的矜持，讓我想起
長江巫峡懸崖峭壁的神女峯
神女的傳說，讓我想起
春秋戰國思潮的百花齊放
百花的色澤，讓我想起
日本北海道富良野的薰衣草
風中薰衣草翻動的流波，讓我想起
法國普羅斯特的追憶似水年華
年華的流逝，讓我想起
柯錫杰攝影捕捉生命之美的瞬間
瞬間的美學，讓我想起
「等待維納斯」的湛藍海域
海域的神話，讓我想起
愛琴海Cape Sounion的神廟
神廟的石柱，讓我想起
Poseidon和Athena對人類的承諾
雅典娜𠄘諾的橄欖樹，讓我想起
那首經典傳唱的校園民歌
三毛與齊豫的《橄欖樹》
“ 不要問我從哪裡來
我的故鄉在遠方
爲什麼流浪，流浪遠方---“
en: The clouds and mist of Shanlinxi bring to mind
The rolling green hillsides of the Scottish Highlands
The reflection of the mountains around the lake reminds me
New Zealand's South Island, its magnificent fjords and capes
The waves at the headland make me recall
Queen's Head Rock standing alone beneath the sky at Yehliu
The queen's reserve makes me recall
Goddess Peak, on the sheer cliffs of Wu Gorge on the Yangtze
The legend of the goddess brings to mind
The hundred schools of thought blooming in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States eras
The colors of a hundred flowers remind me
The lavender of Furano, Hokkaido, Japan
The rippling waves of lavender turning in the wind remind me
Proust's Remembrance of Things Past, France
The passing of the years makes me recall
Ko Si-Chi's photography captures the fleeting instant of life's beauty
The aesthetics of a fleeting moment remind me
The deep azure waters of "Waiting for Venus"
The myths of the sea remind me
The temple at Cape Sounion on the Aegean Sea
The temple's stone pillars bring to mind
The promise of Poseidon and Athena to mankind
Athena's promised olive tree reminds me of
That classic campus folk song still sung today
San Mao and Chyi Yu's "The Olive Tree"
"Don't ask me where I come from
My hometown lies far away
Why wander, wander so far away---“

zh: 衫林溪的雲霧
是一首歌
陪我遊走遠方
流浪他鄉
en: The clouds and mist of Shanlinxi
It is a song
Accompanying me on wanderings to distant places
Wandering in a foreign land

flow.caption_zh: 杉林溪高山茶園雲霧蒸騰。杉林溪茶區海拔800公尺到1950公尺，

zh: 茶區以杉林溪遊樂區為中心點。年雨量2700公釐，和梨山、阿里山
並列為台灣三大高山茶區。  (攝影/何康隆)
en: The tea-growing area is centered on the Shanlinxi recreation area. Annual rainfall is 2,700 millimeters, along with Lishan and Alishan
ranked among Taiwan's three great high-mountain tea regions.  (Photography / Ho Kang-lung)

flow.caption_zh: 蘇格蘭高地雲霧籠罩下的青翠山坡。 (攝影/何康隆)

zh: 蘇格蘭高地峻嶺起伏，山谷翠綠綿延，湖水掩映，雨霧煙嵐時起時散，清凄幽微的民謠傳說迴蕩其中，自有一縷動人心弦的迷濛詩意。羅莽湖畔《Loch Lomond 》，安娜羅荔  《Annie Laurie》和我的邦妮《My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean》都是傳唱已久的蘇格蘭民謠， 每首歌都有人物故事的背景。
en: The peaks of the Scottish Highlands rise and fall, green valleys stretch on, lakes glimmer among them, and rain-mist and haze gather and scatter by turns; within them echo folk songs and legends, clear, plaintive, and faint, carrying their own thread of a heart-stirring, misty poetry. 'Loch Lomond,' 'Annie Laurie,' and 'My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean' are all Scottish folk songs long sung and passed down, each carrying the background of a story and its characters.

flow.caption_zh: 野柳女王岩。 台灣東北海岸綫。 (攝影繪制/何康隆)

zh: 「潮起潮落 / 五千年的風姿 / 孤獨又寂寞 / 為眺望遠天的渺茫 /
召喚昔日的承諾 / 錯過了無數的春花秋月 / 美麗的夢 /
留下美麗的憂愁 / 歲月流逝 / 容顏岩化 / 但是驛動的心 /
也能凝結成石嗎？」      -- (何康隆詩《野柳女王岩》第一節)
en: "Tides rise, tides fall / five thousand years of grace and bearing / lonely and solitary / gazing into the far, hazy sky /
Summoning the promises of yesterday / missing countless springs of flowers and autumns of moons / a beautiful dream /
Leaving behind a beautiful sorrow / the years slip away / the face turns to stone / yet the restless heart /
Can it too congeal into stone?"      -- (from Ho Kang-lung's poem "Queen's Head Rock at Yehliu," first stanza)

points.zh: 長江巫山的神女峰，又名望霞峰、仙女峰、堪稱巫山十二峰之最。一根巨石突兀於青峰雲霞之中，宛若一個亭亭玉立、美麗動人的少女，故名神女峰。長江巫峽的神女峰神話主要圍繞著天上的瑤姬仙女下凡，她被巫峽美景吸引，又憐憫當地百姓受水患之苦，便化作石峰，日日迎朝霞送晚霞，為當地帶來福祉。而與楚懐王的「巫山雲雨」情緣神話故事交織，使其成為「世間最多情的石頭」；神女峰形似亭亭玉立少女，傳說為王母第十三個女兒。其故事也與屈原《九歌·山鬼》傳說相連，充滿浪漫與神秘色彩。
points.en: Goddess Peak of Wushan on the Yangtze River, also known as Wangxia Peak or Immortal Maiden Peak, is regarded as the finest of the Twelve Peaks of Wushan. A single massive rock rises abruptly amid the green peaks and clouds, resembling a slender, graceful, and beautiful young woman standing tall — hence the name Goddess Peak. The legend of Goddess Peak in the Wushan Gorge of the Yangtze centers on the immortal maiden Yao Ji descending from heaven; drawn by the beauty of the Wushan scenery, and taking pity on the local people suffering from floods, she transformed into a stone peak, greeting the morning glow and seeing off the evening glow each day, bringing blessings to the region. This story is intertwined with the legend of King Huai of Chu's romantic tryst — the tale of 'clouds and rain over Wushan' — making her 'the most passionate stone in the world.' Goddess Peak, shaped like a slender, graceful maiden, is said in legend to be the thirteenth daughter of the Queen Mother of the West. Her story is also linked to the legend of the Mountain Spirit in Qu Yuan's 'Nine Songs,' filled with romance and mystery.

zh: 日本北海道富良野薰衣草。世界四大薰衣草產地為法國普羅旺斯、日本北海道、俄羅斯高加索山與中國伊犁。富良野的薰衣草是以深淺紫色𤔡主調，偶而也有異色交織，紛繁其間。
en: Lavender of Furano, Hokkaido, Japan. The world's four great lavender-producing regions are Provence in France, Hokkaido in Japan, the Caucasus Mountains in Russia, and Yili in China. The lavender of Furano is dominated by shades of deep and light purple, though occasionally other colors weave through, adding rich variety.

points.zh: 《追憶似水年華》是法國作家馬塞爾·普魯斯特（1871年—1922年）的作品，以其長度及意識流手法而著名。這部作品細膩刻畫出19世紀末、20世紀初的法國上流社會和文人雅士，從單純地描寫人類社會轉向對人類心理情緒的分析，完成了在文學作品中對人類情感的第一次成熟地剖析，開「意識流」小說之先河，成爲文學史上新的文學形式發軔的標識。作品的總體構架是敘述者對所經歷的往事的回顧，而這種回顧是與遺忘的一種抗爭。同時這部作品是第一部以記敘一部作品的誕生爲題材的著作，普魯斯特認爲人的生活只有在回憶中才形成「真實的生活」，「回憶中的生活比當時當地的現實生活更為現實」；安得烈·莫羅亞在序中就提到：「唯一真實的樂園是人們失去的樂園」，而「幸福的歲月是失去的歲月」。   (摘自維基百科)
points.en: "In Search of Lost Time" is a work by the French writer Marcel Proust (1871-1922), renowned for its length and its stream-of-consciousness technique. This work portrays with great subtlety the French upper class and literary circles of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, shifting from a straightforward depiction of human society toward an analysis of human psychology and emotion, thereby achieving the first mature dissection of human feeling in a literary work and opening the way for the "stream of consciousness" novel—becoming a landmark of a new literary form in literary history. The overall structure of the work is the narrator's retrospective review of past experiences he has lived through, and this act of retrospection is itself a struggle against forgetting. At the same time, this work is the first to take the birth of a work itself as its subject matter; Proust believed that human life becomes "true life" only in memory, that "life as recalled in memory is more real than the reality lived at that time and place." André Maurois notes in his preface: "The only true paradise is the paradise we have lost," and "the happy years are the lost years." (Excerpted from Wikipedia)

flow.caption_zh: 柯錫杰 : 「等待維納斯」。 希臘，1979。 攝影

zh: 詩人鄭愁予當時看了這張照片，便言: 「啊! 愛琴海是維納斯出現的地方，你在等待維納斯啊! 」這幅柯錫傑本人尚不知如何命題的作品，便以此言命名。目前台南成功大學醫學院成杏廳藝術牆懸掛此張作品。。
en: When the poet Cheng Chou-yu saw this photograph at the time, he said: 'Ah! The Aegean is where Venus appeared -- you are waiting for Venus!' This work, which the photographer Ke Hsi-chieh himself had not yet known how to title, was named after these words. This photograph now hangs on the art wall of the Chengxing Hall at the College of Medicine, National Cheng Kung University, Tainan.

points.zh: 柯錫杰 (1929-2020) 以「心象攝影」膾炙國際藝壇的攝影大師，被譽為「臺灣現代攝影第一人」。柯錫杰十分重視攝影的構思和心情，曾𤔡了拍一張愛琴海的照片，等待多時，最後只按了一次快門，而這張作品即是《等待維納斯》。此作對著海，天，屋宇取景，簡靜明朗的畫面，展現攝影師靜觀自得的瀟灑。簡單的畫面構成元素，奇妙的呈現幾何造形的組合，三度空間的縱深霎時被消解，展現出現實的一種幻象美。幾何的造型來自不同色塊的分布，讓此寧靜的景象如同抽象畫一般，澴麗的色彩，對比鮮明，將景物本身實存的自然特徵凝結到最小，成為純粹的色彩對話。此作，展現柯錫杰於1970, 1980年代，引領台灣影像表現的「心象攝影」風格，以外在景像的取景鋪陳內在心緒的抒發，以精確的技術與美感，傳達出文學「詩的意境」與美學「畫的質感」。使用「轉染法」的攝影作品，大幅提升了彩色攝影的藝術層次，引起專業攝影界極大的迴響。此時期的系列作品在台灣展出時更造成一股旋風，也為台灣現代攝影界帶來深遠的影響。
points.en: Ko Si-chi (1929–2020), a master photographer celebrated internationally for his "psychological imagery photography," was hailed as "the first man of modern Taiwanese photography." Ko placed great importance on the conception and mood of photography; it is said that in order to capture a single photograph of the Aegean Sea, he waited a long time and finally pressed the shutter only once — and that photograph is 'Waiting for Venus.' Framing the sea, sky, and buildings, this work, with its simple, clear composition, reveals the photographer's calm, self-possessed elegance of quiet observation. Through simple compositional elements, it wondrously produces a combination of geometric forms; the three-dimensional depth is instantly dissolved, revealing a kind of illusory beauty within reality. The geometric forms arise from the distribution of different blocks of color, so that this tranquil scene appears almost like an abstract painting — its brilliant colors, sharply contrasted, condense the actual natural features of the scenery down to their barest minimum, becoming a pure dialogue of color. This work displays the "psychological imagery photography" style through which Ko led Taiwanese photographic expression in the 1970s and 1980s, using external scenery to lay out and express inner emotion, conveying through precise technique and aesthetic sense the literary "poetic mood" and the artistic "painterly texture." His photographic works using the "dye transfer" process greatly elevated the artistic level of color photography, drawing enormous response from the professional photography world. This series of works, when exhibited in Taiwan during this period, caused a sensation and had a profound influence on Taiwan's modern photography community.

flow.caption_zh: 蘇尼翁海岬 (Cape Sounion)又有稱蘇尼翁角，位於希臘雅典城南70公里, 是希臘阿提卡半島(Attica)最南端的一個三面環水的岬角。在岬角的最高峰有一座供奉著海神波塞冬的古希臘神廟即波塞冬神廟-（Temple of Poseidon）。波賽頓是愛琴海海員和漁民崇拜的一個希臘神明，也是奧林匹斯十二主神之一。 建於雅典黃金時期（約公元前444-440年），以其宏偉的多立克柱式建築和矗立於65米高懸崖邊的壯麗海景聞名，是雅典衛城帕特農神廟 (供奉女神雅典娜) 同時期的重要遺址。此處被雅典人視為雅典娜和波塞冬的聖地，如今這裡已成為雅典觀賞愛琴海和日落的最佳地點。  (攝影/何康隆)

points.zh: 希臘神話:希臘眾神要為一座新建城市取名字。海神波賽頓（Poseidon）和智慧女神雅典娜（Athena）都想當這座城市的守護神。於是眾神決定辦一場「比賽」，看誰送給人類的禮物最有價值。波賽頓一杖插地，湧出了一股海水和一匹飛馬，象徵力量與海上霸權。雅典娜則獻上了一棵橄欖樹，象徵和平、智慧與永續的生活。衆神思考後認為，橄欖樹能提供食物、油、木材，比戰爭的力量，更能讓城市長久繁榮。於是，女神雅典娜獲勝！這座城市便以她的名字命名為雅典（Athens）
points.en: Greek mythology: the gods of Greece wanted to name a newly built city. Poseidon, god of the sea, and Athena, goddess of wisdom, both wished to become the city's patron deity. So the gods decided to hold a "contest" to see whose gift to humankind would be more valuable. Poseidon struck the ground with his trident, and forth gushed seawater and a winged horse, symbolizing strength and mastery of the sea. Athena, in turn, offered an olive tree, symbolizing peace, wisdom, and a sustainable life. After deliberation, the gods concluded that the olive tree, which could provide food, oil, and timber, would bring the city lasting prosperity more surely than the power of war. And so the goddess Athena won! The city was thus named Athens, after her.

zh: 《The Dispute of Minerva (Athena) and Neptune (Poseidon) 》, Noël Hallé (1711-1781), 油畫, 1748, 法國羅浮宮(Musée du Louvre) 。海神波賽頓（Poseidon）和智慧女神雅典娜（Athena）的競賽。雅典娜以獻上橄𣟂樹嬴得雅典城守護神之尊。
en: "The Dispute of Minerva (Athena) and Neptune (Poseidon)", Noel Halle (1711-1781), oil painting, 1748, the Louvre (Musee du Louvre), France. The contest between the sea god Poseidon and the goddess of wisdom Athena. Athena won the honor of patron deity of the city of Athens by offering the olive tree.

flow.caption_zh: 《 橄欖樹 》 詞/三毛  曲/李泰祥  原唱：齊豫

zh: 「不要問我從哪裡來 / 我的故鄉在遠方 / 為什麼流浪 / 流浪遠方 / 流浪 / 為了天空飛翔的小鳥 / 為了山間輕流的小溪 / 為了寬闊的草原 / 流浪遠方 / 流浪 / 還有還有 / 為了夢中的橄欖樹 橄欖樹 / 不要問我從哪裡來 / 我的故鄉在遠方 / 為什麼流浪 / 為什麼流浪 /  流浪遠方 / 流浪為了我 / 夢中的橄欖樹 」
en: "Don't ask me where I come from / My hometown is far away / Why do I wander / Wander far away / Wander / For the little bird flying in the sky / For the small stream flowing gently through the mountains / For the wide open grasslands / Wander far away / Wander / And also, and also / For the olive tree, the olive tree, in my dreams / Don't ask me where I come from / My hometown is far away / Why do I wander / Why do I wander / Wander far away / I wander for / the olive tree in my dreams"

points.zh:
《橄欖樹》是華語世界極具代表性的抒情歌曲，由三毛作詞、李泰祥作曲。歌曲以反覆追問「不要問我從哪裡來／我的故鄉在遠方」開場，旋即拋出「為什麼流浪」的核心命題，將個人生命的出走化為一場精神與靈魂的遠行。歌中的「橄欖樹」並非具體地理之物，而是象徵理想、信念與內在安身之所，一個在行走中尋找、在孤獨中堅持的目標。旋律質樸而深遠，近乎吟唱，承載著淡淡的鄉愁與不屈的自由意志；詞意簡潔卻層層回響，把漂泊者的孤獨轉化為自我確認的力量。正因如此，《橄欖樹》不只是一首思鄉歌，更是一首關於「為何而行」的人生之歌：即使前路漫長、歸處未明，也要循著心中的橄欖樹，繼續走下去。

胡德夫&那英《橄榄树》| 琴声流淌于天地间，隔空合唱呼唤远方归来 |
【橄欖樹】外國女生翻唱 ～ 音色甜美空靈
Singing Beautiful Chinese Song, "The Olive Tree"
Chyi Yu-The Olive Tree / 橄榄树/ Gan Lan Shu. With Eng/Chinese subs
橄榄树/Olive Tree/二胡：田宇
points.en:
"The Olive Tree" is one of the most representative lyrical songs in the Chinese-speaking world, with lyrics by Sanmao and music by Li Tai-hsiang. The song opens with the repeated, questioning refrain "Don't ask me where I come from / my hometown is far away," then immediately raises the central question of "why wander," turning the departure of an individual life into a spiritual and soulful journey. The "olive tree" in the song is not a specific geographic place, but a symbol of ideals, faith, and an inner resting place—a goal sought while walking, held onto in solitude. The melody is simple yet far-reaching, almost chant-like, carrying a faint homesickness together with an unyielding will toward freedom; the wording is spare yet resonates in layer upon layer, transforming the wanderer's loneliness into a force of self-affirmation. For this reason, "The Olive Tree" is not merely a song of homesickness, but a song about "why we go on"—even if the road ahead is long and the destination unclear, one must follow the olive tree in one's heart and keep walking.
